The X-Y Position Indicator for a Display System was the original name given to the device invented by Douglas Engelbart in the 1960s. This device is now universally known as the computer mouse.

All three agents agree on this answer with high confidence (0.93-0.95), and this is indeed correct. The patent filed by Engelbart in 1967 used the formal name "X-Y Position Indicator for a Display System," but the device quickly became known by its informal nickname "mouse" due to its appearance (the cord resembling a tail).

Answer: Mouse
Confidence: 0.95
